record.title: Guyana’s Brazil-frontier COVID travel restriction with weekly goods exceptions, 2020–2021
record.scope: Guyanese restriction on ordinary cross-border land travel at Lethem/Bonfim, with controlled essential exchanges
record.direction: Guyana-administered cross-border travel; entry from Brazil is directly documented.
record.movement: Ordinary travellers and cross-border trading communities; essential supplies were handled through exceptions.
record.exceptions: Thursday goods and limited shopping exchanges; October relaxation added Friday personal travel subject to health conditions.
record.imposing_authority: Government of Guyana and regional border/health authorities
record.enforcement: Official crossing restrictions and requested river patrols; informal river crossings were reported.
record.consequences: Local businesses reported hardship; October relaxation followed pressure from regional leaders and traders.
record.relationship: Resolves lead AM-L02. Distinct imposing authority from Brazil’s AM019; excludes Guyana–Suriname ferry AM034. Later weekday/daily extensions are phases, not new events.
record.status_observation: Status limited to dated evidence; no claim of present closure.
record.official_rationale: Limit transmission of COVID-19 across the Brazil frontier.
record.context: Guyanese measures followed Brazil’s own entry restriction; these are separate decisions on the same frontier.
record.uncertainty: Guyanese start day not resolved; Brazil’s March 19 date is not copied. October 1 is a limited personal-travel relaxation, not full reopening. Reports vary on vaccination/PCR formulation and Friday hours, which are not asserted exactly. Stabroek’s retrospective 19 May 2020 onset conflicts with the official 27 March statement that travel was already suspended; it is not used to date onset.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. March 2020 to limited October 1, 2021 reopening; no exact day count.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Government confirms travel suspension; local REO account confirms measures.
March 2020 only; March 26/27 reports do not establish first closure day.

Hierarchical coding: see Rationale coding for subcategories, attribution and phases. The recorded rationale and claim assessment support the selected subcategories. All applicable broad categories are retained together; no primary rationale is imposed. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): COVID-19 containment.
Takutu bridge personal travel with limited goods/minister-authorized exceptions.
Limited relaxation does not establish full reopening or continuous universal closure.
